subject: CypressAI: Post-incident delivery, corrective plan, and leadership assurance
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@cypressai.com>, Tom Harper <tom.harper@cypressai.com>
Cc: CypressAI Infra <infra@cypressai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: CypressAI incident: RCA delivery and proposed corrective actions

Hi Elena, Tom —

Thanks again for your patience on Friday's throughput spike. Attached is the post-incident package: a short RCA, the telemetry snapshot we used for the analysis, and our prioritized corrective action plan. High-level summary below: 

- Root cause: cache-thrashing when heavy batched long-context requests coincided with a spike in concurrent short inference calls; the KV cache eviction strategy and a suboptimal batching threshold created repeated cold-starts.
- Impact window: 2026-02-06 16:12–16:47 UTC — latency +4x median, error rate increased from 0.6% to 3.9% for affected routes.
- Customer visible effects: delayed page loads and a 15% rise in failed streaming responses for your OCR pipeline.

Proposed next steps (we included owner and ETA in the attachment):
1) Immediate mitigation (Karthik): tune batching thresholds + enable sticky small-request lanes — deploy within 24 hours.
2) Medium-term (Ben): revise KV cache eviction and introduce per-tenant soft caches — patch in 5 business days, full rollout over 3 weeks.
3) Compensation proposal (Marissa): SLA credit calculation and a short-term dedicated pool while patching finishes.

We recognize this required executive attention; Marissa and I will coordinate the customer-facing timeline. I'm available for a readout today if helpful.

Attachments: cypressai_incident_rca_20260210.pdf, throughput_counters_snapshot_20260210.csv

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

--

Subject: Re: CypressAI incident: RCA delivery and proposed corrective actions

Folks — quick technical update ahead of the 11am readout: 

Summary of fix approach (high level):
- Immediate: enable request-class segregation (sticky lanes) and bump batching threshold to avoid interleaving large long-context requests with short ones. This is a config change and hot-deployable with zero restarts; we will run canary traffic to a subset of nodes in the dedicated pool for 2 hours before wider rollout. ETA: 22 hours for config and verification.
- Near-term patch: adjust KV eviction policy to be time-weighted + tenant-awareness to prevent cross-tenant cache thrash. This requires a rolling restart of inference workers; we expect the restart window to be 3–4 minutes per worker. We'll schedule rolling restarts during low-traffic windows and use canary validations. ETA: 5 business days for patch + staged rollout.
- Observability: create a dedicated per-tenant cache hit-rate dashboard and an automated alert if hit-rate drops 20% vs baseline.

I've attached a preliminary patch diff (kx-fix-branch-diff.patch) for review. Ben will lead validation.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — short validation plan from my side for the readout and the next 48 hours: 

1) Today (post-readout): run 2-hour canary with sticky lanes on 10% of CypressAI traffic; capture latency distribution, error-rate, and cache hit-rate.
2) If canary shows >60% reduction in high-latency tail and error-rate returns to baseline, promote config change to 50% and continue staged rollout.
3) Deploy kx-fix-branch to a non-prod cluster and exercise with the same workload for 24 hours; validate rolling restart duration and error surface.
4) If validated, schedule rolling restart into production in 5 business days with 4-hour low-traffic window per region.

I'll attach the patch diff (kx-fix-branch-diff.patch) and a short validation checklist. I'll also capture a short video of the canary run results for the customer.

-Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena —

Following the readout, attached is our proposed compensation calculation and a short-term dedicated pool spec while the patch rolls out: 
- Compensation: we propose a one-off credit equal to 10% of February projected usage (pre-incident baseline). Template and DocuSign link for approval: https://docs.redwood/slo/credit-approval-template
- Dedicated pool: 2x the instance profile you're currently on for 72 hours (isolated tenant pool) + observation and automatic rollback if we detect regressions. Cost impact and implementation timeline included in the attached.

If you approve, we can issue the credit immediately and spin up the dedicated pool within 4 hours of sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final update: CypressAI assurance, exec pledge, and next-step tracking

Stephanie —

Quick leadership summary and ask: we completed the customer readout and have the following commitments and tracking in place for CypressAI: 

- Immediate: canary sticky lanes deployed (10% traffic) — initial telemetry looks positive (median latency down 28%, tail improvements ongoing).
- Next 24–48 hours: complete the 2-hour canary + expanded 50% rollout if validated.
- 5 business days: full patch deployment of KV eviction logic with scheduled rolling restarts; we will minimize worker restart impact to ~3 minutes per worker and perform during the pre-agreed low-traffic window.
- Compensation: Marissa proposed a 10% usage credit for February; CypressAI has the DocuSign link and indicated probable approval.

Requested action: please note this incident for exec visibility. If you can join a 15-minute sync tomorrow at 09:30 PST to sign off on the communication plan with legal/comms, that would be helpful.

Tracking artifacts: https://drive.redwood/company/rca/CypressAI-20260210 and HubSpot deal D-78321 has the action checklist.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
